title: The popular version. Unix time began in 1970.
description:
Unix time began in 1970. That is where the clock starts now. It is not where it started.

Dated 3 November 1971. It counted time from 1 January 1971, not 1970.

The first edition counted time in sixtieths of a second, as a 32 bit number.

The manual admits it would run out. Its own BUGS section says 2**32 sixtieths of a second is only about 2.5 years.

In 1973 the units became full seconds. Counted from the 1970 New Year. Wikipedia says engineers picked that date arbitrarily, as a convenient one.

The zero point was a patch.

Sources:
- https://www.nokia.com/bell-labs/about/dennis-m-ritchie/1stEdman.html: read in full (Dennis Ritchie's page for the first edition Unix Programmer's Manual, hosted by Nokia Bell Labs). Established the manual is dated 3 November 1971, that time was measured in sixtieths of a second since 1 Jan. 1971 as a 32 bit quantity, the manual's own BUGS line that 2**32 sixtieths of a second is only about 2.5 years, and that this was later patched more than once before units became full seconds dating from the 1970 New Year in 1973.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time: History section read. Established that the current epoch of 1 January 1970 was selected arbitrarily by Unix engineers as a convenient date (citing Wired, 2001), and that the precision was changed to seconds to avoid short term overflow.
- https://minnie.tuhs.org/mailman3/hyperkitty/list/tuhs@tuhs.org/thread/MVO2V2Y3OTFEBLLM3ABRP2FKYJOHLPCG: read in full (TUHS mailing list, May 2009). Corroborated the first edition epoch of 1 January 1971 and that the later epoch was set for the fourth edition. The poster says the manual texts are paraphrased, so no wording is taken from it.
